description:
Why: fz has is_binary/1 but no is_bitstring/1 (Kernel lists it in Elixir; it is a guard). Without it, a library cannot tell a non-byte-aligned bitstring from a non-binary, so :binary.copy(<<1::3>>) says 'not a binary' where Elixir says '1st argument: is a bitstring (expected a binary)' (fz-nml.11, PR #628).
Investigate first: how is_binary is resolved as a guard and type test (src/runtime_type_predicate.rs Binaries axis, compiler2 types is_binary), and whether fz's type world distinguishes bitstring from binary. Add is_bitstring/1 by the same authority as is_binary, not as a second mechanism; on all three paths, in guards and in bodies.
Acceptance: an oracle fixture in a free fixture block shows is_bitstring and is_binary over binaries, bitstrings and non-bitstrings, matching Elixir; lib/binary.fz's complaint uses it, and 01338's oracle gains the <<1::3>> case.
title: is_bitstring/1 is a guard, and :binary raises Elixir's 'is a bitstring' wording
